subject: Private monitoring export orchestration — SIEM + trace hooks (Globex)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private monitoring export orchestration — SIEM + trace hooks (Globex)

Hi Sonia / Infra team,

Following our call yesterday, putting the proposed export/orchestration checklist into an email so we have a clear acceptance path for Globex private deployment. Goal: export logs/metrics/traces from the private Redwood runtime to Globex's SIEM stack (Splunk/HEC) and tracing backend (OTLP/Lightstep) with auditability and minimal egress footprint.

High-level asks from Globex we discussed:
- Encrypted delivery to their on-prem SIEM gateway (mTLS preferred)
- Per-route sampling controls and trace hook metadata (service, model, request-id)
- Mapping token-level telemetry to their ingestion schema (fields + timestamp format)
- Retention and evidence export package for 90-day compliance audits

Open items we need answers for before we schedule a dry-run:
1) HEC endpoint, port, and mTLS cert distribution process
2) Preferred timestamp format (ISO8601 w/ ms or epoch-ms) and time zone normalization
3) Maximum sustained ingest rate they can accept (events/sec) for throttling config
4) Any approved egress IP ranges or proxy hostname we must send through

Attached: redwood_export_mapping_v1.csv (sample field mapping) and a tiny sample logs bundle from a staging run.

Proposed next steps:
- Globex infra sends HEC details + accepted TLS fingerprint by Mon, Mar 12
- Redwood team drafts firewall + batching config and run a 2-hour smoke ingestion window
- Capture evidence bundle (signed manifest) and run retention export test

Thanks — I can own the runbook and evidence artifact if you confirm the infra details above.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions (North America)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private monitoring export orchestration — SIEM + trace hooks (Globex)

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the items below and adding details from our side.

Answers to open items:
1) HEC endpoint: https://siem-gw.globex.local:8088/hec (internal DNS only). We require mTLS; we'll provide a CA bundle and a short-lived client cert via our vault process.
2) Timestamp: ISO8601 with millisecond precision, UTC preferred.
3) Max ingest: start with 2,500 events/sec sustained, spikes up to 8k for 30s tolerated (we will monitor). Please ensure batching to avoid per-event TLS overhead.
4) Egress: traffic must originate from a fixed NAT IP range; we will share the CIDR and proxy host by EOD Mon (Mar 12). No direct public IPs allowed.

Security notes:
- All payloads must be encrypted in transit and signed.
- We will require a signed evidence manifest after the smoke window for our audit team.

Questions from infra team (cc'd):
- Do you support OTLP over gRPC for traces or only HTTP/JSON?
- What retry/backoff does your forwarder use for temporary 5xx responses?

We will upload the CA bundle to your shared Drive folder and create a Jira ticket (OPS-9723) for the run.

Sonia
Sonia Patel
Director, Infrastructure
Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: Private monitoring export orchestration — SIEM + trace hooks (Globex)

Sonia / Team — quick tech plan and the minimal config we will exercise during the smoke window.

1) Transport & Protocols- Logs/metrics: HTTP(s) -> Splunk HEC (mTLS). We will use persistent keep-alive connections + 50ms batching window.
- Traces: OTLP/gRPC to Globex trace gateway (we support gRPC and HTTP); prefer gRPC for lower overhead.

2) Auth & Certs- We'll pull client certs from the Vault URL you provide via a one-shot signed request. Cert rotation: our forwarder will rotate certs every 24h if a longer TTL is needed, with zero-downtime handshake.

3) Schema & Mapping- Attached CSV shows our proposed mapping: event_time -> timestamp_iso, model_name -> service.name, request_id -> trace_id/span_id fields.
- We will canonicalize timestamps to UTC in the forwarder and include original-local-tz as event.meta.local_tz.

4) Backpressure & Retry- Exponential backoff with jitter for 5xx, up to 10 retries; we will buffer up to 200MB on disk (configurable). For sustained bursts beyond your 2,500 eps target we will throttle by dropping low-value debug logs first (configurable sample rate).

5) Evidence & Audit- At the end of the smoke run we will create a signed manifest (SHA256 list) of exported files and an ingestion report (counts, latencies, failed events). We'll store the manifest in the shared Drive folder and email the signed artifact.

6) Firewall/Egress- Please provide the NAT CIDR and the proxy FQDN. We'll test via your proxy first. If NAT range is accepted we'll add the IPs to our outbound whitelist.

Smoke window acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- >=95% of events delivered within 10s of emission- No TLS handshake failures >0.5%- Evidence manifest present and verified by Globex security

If this looks right I'll schedule the 2-hour smoke for Thu, Mar 15 09:00-11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Kim
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

All — quick confirmation from the ops side after reviewing the plan. We validated the following during a brief dry-run this morning (via Globex proxy):
- HEC mTLS handshake succeeded using the CA bundle provided. No cert validation errors.
- OTLP/gRPC traces arrived with service.name and trace_id preserved. Sampling metadata included as trace.attributes.model_version.
- Average delivery latency: 320ms (p95 1.2s) for 1,800 eps sustained; spikes tested to 6k eps with backpressure behaving as expected.

Next items before the runbook is 'signed off':
1) Globex to confirm NAT CIDR by EOD today so we can finalize firewall entries.
2) Redwood to add a small ingestion tag field (ingest_origin=redwood-staging) so auditors can identify provenance.
3) Ensure evidence manifest is PGP-signed; we will verify signatures on receipt.

Thanks — once NAT range is confirmed we can proceed with Kimberly's proposed 2-hour smoke window.

Michael Owens
Site Reliability Lead (Partner Integrations)
Acme Cloud Services (on behalf of Globex)
